sanskrit: vibhave na nṛṇāṃ puṇyaṃ svaśaktyā svarjitaṃ satām na yajñair vividhair vipra yathānyāyena saṃcitaiḥ
english: In sheer abundance there is no merit for men; for the good, what is earned righteously by one's own power outweighs, O brāhmaṇa, the fruit gathered through manifold sacrifices.

sanskrit: krodho dānaphalaṃ hanti lobhāt svargaṃ na gacchati nyāyavṛttir hi tapasā dānavit svargam aśnute
english: Anger destroys the fruit of giving, and through greed one does not reach heaven; but the man of righteous conduct, knowing how to give, attains heaven through his austerity.

sanskrit: na rājasūyair bahubhir iṣṭvā vipuladakṣiṇaiḥ na cāśvamedhair bahubhiḥ phalaṃ samam idaṃ tava
english: Not by many Rājasūya sacrifices offered with lavish gifts, nor by many Aśvamedhas, could a fruit be won equal to this of yours.

sanskrit: saktuprasthena hi jito brahmalokas tvayānagha virajo brahmabhavanaṃ gaccha vipra yathecchakam
english: By a measure of barley-meal the world of Brahmā has been won by you, O sinless one; go, O brāhmaṇa, to the stainless abode of Brahmā as you wish.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ vo dvijaśreṣṭha divyaṃ yānam upasthitam ārohata yathākāmaṃ dharmo 'smi dvija paśya mām
english: For all of you, O best of the twice-born, a celestial chariot now stands ready; mount it at your pleasure. I am Dharma, O brāhmaṇa—behold me.

sanskrit: pāvito hi tvayā deho loke kīrtiḥ sthirā ca te sabhāryaḥ sahaputraś ca sasnuṣaś ca divaṃ vraja
english: By you the body has been purified, and your fame stands firm in the world; with your wife, with your son, and with your daughter-in-law, go to heaven.

sanskrit: ity uktavākyo dharmeṇa yānam āruhya sa dvijaḥ sabhāryaḥ sasutaś cāpi sasnuṣaś ca divaṃ yayau
english: Thus addressed by Dharma, that brāhmaṇa mounted the chariot and, with his wife, his son, and his daughter-in-law, went up to heaven.

sanskrit: tasmin vipre gate svargaṃ sasute sasnuṣe tadā bhāryācaturthe dharmajñe tato 'haṃ niḥsṛto bilāt
english: When that brāhmaṇa, knower of dharma, had gone to heaven with his son, his daughter-in-law, and his wife as the fourth, I then came forth from my burrow.

sanskrit: tatas tu saktugandhena kledena salilasya ca divyapuṣpāvamardāc ca sādhor dānalavaiś ca taiḥ viprasya tapasā tasya śiro me kāñcanīkṛtam
english: And then, by the scent of that barley-meal, by the moisture of the water, by the crushing of celestial flowers, by those very fragments of the good man's gift, and by that brāhmaṇa's austerity, my head was turned to gold.

sanskrit: tasya satyābhisaṃdhasya sūkṣmadānena caiva ha śarīrārdhaṃ ca me viprāḥ śātakumbhamayaṃ kṛtam paśyatedaṃ suvipulaṃ tapasā tasya dhīmataḥ
english: And by the slender gift of that man true to his word, half my body too, O brāhmaṇas, was made of gold. Behold this vast transformation, wrought by the austerity of that wise one.

sanskrit: katham evaṃvidhaṃ me syād anyat pārśvam iti dvijāḥ tapovanāni yajñāṃś ca hṛṣṭo 'bhyemi punaḥ punaḥ
english: 'How might my other side too become like this?'—so thinking, O twice-born, eagerly I visit again and again the groves of penance and the sites of sacrifice.

sanskrit: yajñaṃ tv aham imaṃ śrutvā kururājasya dhīmataḥ āśayā parayā prāpto na cāhaṃ kāñcanīkṛtaḥ
english: Hearing of this sacrifice of the wise king of the Kurus, I came with the highest hope—yet I have not been turned to gold.

sanskrit: tato mayoktaṃ tad vākyaṃ prahasya dvijasattamāḥ saktuprasthena yajño 'yaṃ saṃmito neti sarvathā
english: Therefore, O best of the twice-born, laughing, I spoke these words: this sacrifice is by no means the equal of that measure of barley-meal.

sanskrit: saktuprasthalavais tair hi tadāhaṃ kāñcanīkṛtaḥ na hi yajño mahān eṣa sadṛśas tair mato mama
english: For by those fragments of the barley-meal I was then turned to gold; this great sacrifice, in my judgment, is not their equal.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā nakulaḥ sarvān yajñe dvijavarāṃs tadā jagāmādarśanaṃ rājan viprās te ca yayur gṛhān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus spoken to all the foremost brāhmaṇas at the sacrifice, the mongoose vanished from sight, O king, and those brāhmaṇas went to their homes.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ mayā parapuraṃjaya yad āścaryam abhūt tasmin vājimedhe mahākratau
english: All this I have related to you, O conqueror of hostile cities—the wonder that came to pass at that great horse-sacrifice.

sanskrit: na vismayas te nṛpate yajñe kāryaḥ kathaṃ cana ṛṣikoṭisahasrāṇi tapobhir ye divaṃ gatāḥ
english: You should feel no astonishment at all, O king, at the sacrifice; for thousands upon tens of millions of sages have gone to heaven through their austerities.

sanskrit: adrohaḥ sarvabhūteṣu saṃtoṣaḥ śīlam ārjavam tapo damaś ca satyaṃ ca dānaṃ ceti samaṃ matam
english: Harmlessness toward all beings, contentment, good conduct, uprightness, austerity, self-restraint, truth, and giving—these are held to be of equal worth.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca yajñe saktā nṛpatayas tapaḥsaktā maharṣayaḥ śāntivyavasitā viprāḥ śamo dama iti prabho
english: Janamejaya said: Kings are devoted to sacrifice, the great sages devoted to austerity, and the brāhmaṇas set upon peace—'tranquillity and self-restraint,' so they say, O lord.

sanskrit: tasmād yajñaphalais tulyaṃ na kiṃ cid iha vidyate iti me vartate buddhis tathā caitad asaṃśayam
english: 'Therefore nothing here is found to equal the fruits of sacrifice'—so my mind has held, and so without doubt it seemed to me.

sanskrit: yajñair iṣṭvā hi bahavo rājāno dvijasattama iha kīrtiṃ parāṃ prāpya pretya svargam ito gatāḥ
english: For many kings, O best of the twice-born, having worshipped with sacrifices and won the highest fame here, departed hence to heaven after death.

sanskrit: devarājaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ kratubhir bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ devarājyaṃ mahātejāḥ prāptavān akhilaṃ vibhuḥ
english: The thousand-eyed king of the gods, mighty in splendour, the all-powerful one, attained by sacrifices with abundant gifts the entire sovereignty over the gods.

sanskrit: yathā yudhiṣṭhiro rājā bhīmārjunapuraḥsaraḥ sadṛśo devarājena samṛddhyā vikrameṇa ca
english: Just as King Yudhiṣṭhira, with Bhīma and Arjuna at his head, was the equal of the king of the gods in prosperity and in valour.

sanskrit: atha kasmāt sa nakulo garhayām āsa taṃ kratum aśvamedhaṃ mahāyajñaṃ rājñas tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Then why did that mongoose disparage that rite, the Aśvamedha, the great sacrifice of that high-souled king?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yajñasya vidhim agryaṃ vai phalaṃ caiva nararṣabha gadataḥ śṛṇu me rājan yathāvad iha bhārata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The foremost rule of sacrifice and its fruit, O bull among men, hear from me as I tell it truly here, O king, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: purā śakrasya yajataḥ sarva ūcur maharṣayaḥ ṛtvikṣu karmavyagreṣu vitate yajñakarmaṇi
english: Long ago, while Śakra was sacrificing, all the great sages spoke out, when the priests were busy with their tasks and the rite of sacrifice was under way.

sanskrit: hūyamāne tathā vahnau hotre bahuguṇānvite deveṣv āhūyamāneṣu sthiteṣu paramarṣiṣu
english: As the oblation was poured into the fire, the office of the hotṛ priest being richly endowed, the gods being summoned, and the supreme sages standing by.

sanskrit: supratītais tadā vipraiḥ svāgamaiḥ susvanair nṛpa aśrāntaiś cāpi laghubhir adhvaryuvṛṣabhais tathā
english: By the brāhmaṇas then well assured, versed in their own scriptures and clear of voice, O king, and by the foremost adhvaryu priests, tireless and deft.

sanskrit: ālambhasamaye tasmin gṛhīteṣu paśuṣv atha maharṣayo mahārāja saṃbabhūvuḥ kṛpānvitāḥ
english: At that moment of immolation, when the sacrificial animals had been seized, the great sages, O mighty king, were filled with compassion.

sanskrit: tato dīnān paśūn dṛṣṭvā ṛṣayas te tapodhanāḥ ūcuḥ śakraṃ samāgamya nāyaṃ yajñavidhiḥ śubhaḥ
english: Then, seeing the wretched animals, those sages rich in austerity came up to Śakra and said: 'This rule of sacrifice is not auspicious.'

sanskrit: apavijñānam etat te mahāntaṃ dharmam icchataḥ na hi yajñe paśugaṇā vidhidṛṣṭāḥ puraṃdara
english: 'This is a misunderstanding on your part, who desire the great dharma; for herds of animals at a sacrifice are not what is sanctioned by the rule, O Purandara.'

sanskrit: dharmopaghātakas tv eṣa samārambhas tava prabho nāyaṃ dharmakṛto dharmo na hiṃsā dharma ucyate
english: 'This undertaking of yours, O lord, is a destroyer of dharma; this is no dharma born of righteousness—violence is not called dharma.'

sanskrit: āgamenaiva te yajñaṃ kurvantu yadi hecchasi vidhidṛṣṭena yajñena dharmas te sumahān bhavet
english: 'Let them perform your sacrifice by scripture alone, if you wish it; by a sacrifice sanctioned by the rule your dharma would be very great.'

sanskrit: yaja bījaiḥ sahasrākṣa trivarṣaparamoṣitaiḥ eṣa dharmo mahāñ śakra cintyamāno 'dhigamyate
english: 'Sacrifice with seeds, O thousand-eyed one, kept stored at most for three years; this is great dharma, O Śakra, attained when rightly pondered.'

sanskrit: śatakratus tu tad vākyam ṛṣibhis tattvadarśibhiḥ uktaṃ na pratijagrāha mānamohavaśānugaḥ
english: But Śatakratu did not accept that counsel spoken by the sages who perceive the truth, for he was in thrall to pride and delusion.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vivādaḥ sumahāñ jajñe śakramaharṣiṇām jaṅgamaiḥ sthāvarair vāpi yaṣṭavyam iti bhārata
english: A very great dispute arose between Śakra and the great sages—whether sacrifice should be made with moving creatures or with things that do not move, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: te tu khinnā vivādena ṛṣayas tattvadarśinaḥ tataḥ saṃdhāya śakreṇa papracchur nṛpatiṃ vasum
english: But those sages who perceive the truth, weary of the dispute, then, by agreement with Śakra, put the question to King Vasu.

sanskrit: mahābhāga kathaṃ yajñeṣv āgamo nṛpate smṛtaḥ yaṣṭavyaṃ paśubhir medhyair atho bījair ajair api
english: 'O greatly blessed king, what is the scriptural tradition handed down for sacrifices? Should one sacrifice with sacred animals, or rather with seeds and with that which is unborn?'

sanskrit: tac chrutvā tu vacas teṣām avicārya balābalam yathopanītair yaṣṭavyam iti provāca pārthivaḥ
english: Hearing that question of theirs, without weighing its strength and weakness, the king declared: 'One should sacrifice with whatever is brought to hand.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā sa nṛpatiḥ praviveśa rasātalam uktveha vitathaṃ rājaṃś cedīnām īśvaraḥ prabhuḥ
english: Having spoken thus, that king sank into the nether world; for he had uttered a falsehood here, O king—that lord and master of the Cedis.

sanskrit: anyāyopagataṃ dravyam atītaṃ yo hy apaṇḍitaḥ dharmābhikāṅkṣī yajate na dharmaphalam aśnute
english: Whoever, being unwise, though longing for dharma, sacrifices with wealth obtained by unrighteous means, gains no fruit of dharma.

sanskrit: dharmavaitaṃsiko yas tu pāpātmā puruṣas tathā dadāti dānaṃ viprebhyo lokaviśvāsakārakam
english: And the man of evil soul who makes a snare of dharma, who gives gifts to brāhmaṇas merely to win the world's trust—

sanskrit: pāpena karmaṇā vipro dhanaṃ labdhvā niraṅkuśaḥ rāgamohānvitaḥ so 'nte kaluṣāṃ gatim āpnute
english: Such an unbridled twice-born, having gained wealth by sinful deed and possessed by passion and delusion, attains in the end a foul course.

sanskrit: tena dattāni dānāni pāpena hatabuddhinā tāni sattvam anāsādya naśyanti vipulāny api
english: The gifts bestowed by that sinful man of ruined judgment, however vast, find no firm ground and perish.

sanskrit: tasyādharmapravṛttasya hiṃsakasya durātmanaḥ dāne na kīrtir bhavati pretya ceha ca durmateḥ
english: For that wicked-minded man given to unrighteousness, the cruel one of evil soul, there is no glory in his giving—neither here nor after death.

sanskrit: api saṃcayabuddhir hi lobhamohavaśaṃgataḥ udvejayati bhūtāni hiṃsayā pāpacetanaḥ
english: Indeed, the man bent on hoarding, in thrall to greed and delusion, of sinful mind, torments living beings with his violence.

sanskrit: evaṃ labdhvā dhanaṃ lobhād yajate yo dadāti ca sa kṛtvā karmaṇā tena na sidhyati durāgamāt
english: He who, having gained wealth thus through greed, sacrifices and gives—by that deed he does not succeed, for it springs from ill-gotten means.

sanskrit: uñchaṃ mūlaṃ phalaṃ śākam udapātraṃ tapodhanāḥ dānaṃ vibhavato dattvā narāḥ svar yānti dharmiṇaḥ
english: Gleaned grain, root, fruit, herb, or a vessel of water, O you rich in austerity—righteous men who give such a gift according to their means go to heaven.

sanskrit: eṣa dharmo mahāṃs tyāgo dānaṃ bhūtadayā tathā brahmacaryaṃ tathā satyam anukrośo dhṛtiḥ kṣamā sanātanasya dharmasya mūlam etat sanātanam
english: This is great dharma: renunciation, giving, and compassion for living beings; chastity, truth, mercy, steadfastness, and forbearance—this is the eternal root of the eternal dharma.

sanskrit: śrūyante hi purā viprā viśvāmitrādayo nṛpāḥ viśvāmitro 'sitaś caiva janakaś ca mahīpatiḥ kakṣasenārṣṭiṣeṇau ca sindhudvīpaś ca pārthivaḥ
english: For we hear, O brāhmaṇas, of kings of old, Viśvāmitra and the rest—Viśvāmitra and Asita, Janaka the lord of earth, Kakṣasena and Ārṣṭiṣeṇa, and Sindhudvīpa the king.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavaḥ siddhiṃ paramikāṃ gatāḥ nṛpāḥ satyaiś ca dānaiś ca nyāyalabdhais tapodhanāḥ
english: These and many other kings, rich in austerity, attained the highest perfection through truth and through gifts gained by righteous means.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā ye cāśritās tapaḥ dānadharmāgninā śuddhās te svargaṃ yānti bhārata
english: Brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras who have taken to austerity—purified by the fire of giving and dharma, they go to heaven, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca dharmāgatena tyāgena bhagavan sarvam asti cet etan me sarvam ācakṣva kuśalo hy asi bhāṣitum
english: Janamejaya said: If, O reverend one, all is attainable through renunciation that comes by righteous means, then declare all this to me, for you are skilled in speaking.

sanskrit: tatoñchavṛtter yad vṛttaṃ saktudāne phalaṃ mahat kathitaṃ me mahad brahmaṃs tathyam etad asaṃśayam
english: The great fruit that came of the gift of barley-meal by one living on gleaned grain has been told me as great, O brāhmaṇa; this is true beyond doubt.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi sarvayajñeṣu niścayaḥ paramo bhavet etad arhasi me vaktuṃ nikhilena dvijarṣabha
english: How then, among all sacrifices, would the supreme certainty be reached? This you ought to tell me in full, O bull among the twice-born.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam agastyasya mahāyajñe purāvṛttam ariṃdama
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: On this they recount too this ancient tale, of what came to pass long ago at the great sacrifice of Agastya, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: purāgastyo mahātejā dīkṣāṃ dvādaśavārṣikīm praviveśa mahārāja sarvabhūtahite rataḥ
english: Long ago, Agastya of great splendour, devoted to the welfare of all beings, entered upon a consecration of twelve years, O mighty king.

sanskrit: tatrāgnikalpā hotāra āsan satre mahātmanaḥ mūlāhārā nirāhārāḥ sāśmakuṭṭā marīcipāḥ
english: At the rite of that high-souled one the officiating priests were like fire itself—living on roots, or taking no food at all, grinding grain with stones, or drinking only the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: parighṛṣṭikā vaighasikāḥ saṃprakṣālās tathaiva ca yatayo bhikṣavaś cātra babhūvuḥ paryavasthitāḥ
english: Some ate only what was ground fine, some only the leavings of others, some kept naught for the morrow; and ascetics and mendicants too were there, stationed all about.

sanskrit: sarve pratyakṣadharmāṇo jitakrodhā jitendriyāḥ dame sthitāś ca te sarve dambhamohavivarjitāḥ
english: All of them had dharma made manifest in them, had conquered anger and subdued their senses; all were established in self-restraint, free of hypocrisy and delusion.

sanskrit: vṛtte śuddhe sthitā nityam indriyaiś cāpy avāhitāḥ upāsate sma taṃ yajñaṃ bhuñjānās te maharṣayaḥ
english: Ever fixed in pure conduct, untroubled by the senses, those great sages attended upon that sacrifice and partook of its food.

sanskrit: yathāśaktyā bhagavatā tad annaṃ samupārjitam tasmin satre tu yat kiṃ cid ayogyaṃ tatra nābhavat tathā hy anekair munibhir mahāntaḥ kratavaḥ kṛtāḥ
english: That food the reverend one had procured according to his power; and at that rite nothing whatever was unfit, for great sacrifices have been performed thus by many sages.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhes tv agastyasya vartamāne mahādhvare na vavarṣa sahasrākṣas tadā bharatasattama
english: But while the great sacrifice of Agastya, of such a kind, was going on, the thousand-eyed one did not send rain, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tataḥ karmāntare rājann agastyasya mahātmanaḥ katheyam abhinirvṛttā munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām
english: Then, in an interval of the rite of the high-souled Agastya, O king, this discourse arose among the sages of disciplined souls.

sanskrit: agastyo yajamāno 'sau dadāty annaṃ vimatsaraḥ na ca varṣati parjanyaḥ katham annaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: 'Agastya, the sacrificer, gives food without grudging; yet the rain-cloud sends no rain—how will there be food?'

sanskrit: satraṃ cedaṃ mahad viprā muner dvādaśavārṣikam na varṣiṣyati devaś ca varṣāṇy etāni dvādaśa
english: 'And this great rite of the sage, O brāhmaṇas, lasts twelve years; and the god will not send rain for these twelve years.'

sanskrit: etad bhavantaḥ saṃcintya maharṣer asya dhīmataḥ agastyasyātitapasaḥ kartum arhanty anugraham
english: 'Considering this, you ought to do a kindness for this wise great sage, Agastya of surpassing austerity.'

sanskrit: ity evam ukte vacane tato 'gastyaḥ pratāpavān provācedaṃ vaco vāgmī prasādya śirasā munīn
english: When these words had been thus spoken, Agastya the mighty, eloquent of speech, won the sages over with a bow of his head and said this:

sanskrit: yadi dvādaśavarṣāṇi na varṣiṣyati vāsavaḥ cintāyajñaṃ kariṣyāmi vidhir eṣa sanātanaḥ
english: 'If for twelve years Vāsava sends no rain, I shall perform the sacrifice of thought; this is the eternal rule.'

sanskrit: yadi dvādaśavarṣāṇi na varṣiṣyati vāsavaḥ vyāyāmenāhariṣyāmi yajñān anyān ativratān
english: 'If for twelve years Vāsava sends no rain, by my own exertion I shall accomplish other sacrifices of surpassing rigour.'

sanskrit: bījayajño mayāyaṃ vai bahuvarṣasamācitaḥ bījaiḥ kṛtaiḥ kariṣye ca nātra vighno bhaviṣyati
english: 'This sacrifice of mine with seeds, gathered over many years—I shall carry it out with prepared seeds, and here there will be no hindrance.'

sanskrit: nedaṃ śakyaṃ vṛthā kartuṃ mama satraṃ kathaṃ cana varṣiṣyatīha vā devo na vā devo bhaviṣyati
english: 'This rite of mine cannot be made vain by any means, whether the god sends rain here or whether he does not.'

sanskrit: atha vābhyarthanām indraḥ kuryān na tv iha kāmataḥ svayam indro bhaviṣyāmi jīvayiṣyāmi ca prajāḥ
english: 'Or else Indra may grant my entreaty—but not by his mere pleasure; I myself shall become Indra and give life to the creatures.'

sanskrit: yo yad āhārajātaś ca sa tathaiva bhaviṣyati viśeṣaṃ caiva kartāsmi punaḥ punar atīva hi
english: 'Whatever each being was born to feed upon, that it shall have just so; and beyond this I shall make abundance, again and again, exceedingly.'

sanskrit: adyeha svarṇam abhyetu yac cānyad vasu durlabham triṣu lokeṣu yac cāsti tad ihāgacchatāṃ svayam
english: 'This day let gold come hither, and whatever other wealth is hard to win; whatever exists in the three worlds, let it come here of its own accord.'

sanskrit: divyāś cāpsarasāṃ saṃghāḥ sagandharvāḥ sakiṃnarāḥ viśvāvasuś ca ye cānye te 'py upāsantu vaḥ sadā
english: 'And the celestial throngs of apsarases, with the gandharvas and the kiṃnaras, Viśvāvasu and the others too—let them ever wait upon you.'

sanskrit: uttarebhyaḥ kurubhyaś ca yat kiṃ cid vasu vidyate sarvaṃ tad iha yajñe me svayam evopatiṣṭhatu svargaṃ svargasadaś caiva dharmaś ca svayam eva tu
english: 'And whatever wealth there is among the Northern Kurus, let it all present itself here of its own accord at my sacrifice—heaven, and the dwellers in heaven, and Dharma himself as well.'

sanskrit: ity ukte sarvam evaitad abhavat tasya dhīmataḥ tatas te munayo dṛṣṭvā munes tasya tapobalam vismitā vacanaṃ prāhur idaṃ sarve mahārthavat
english: When he had spoken thus, all this came to pass for that wise one. Then those sages, beholding the power of that sage's austerity, were amazed and all spoke this word of deep meaning:

sanskrit: prītāḥ sma tava vākyena na tv icchāmas tapovyayam svair eva yajñais tuṣṭāḥ smo nyāyenecchāmahe vayam
english: 'We are pleased by your word, yet we do not wish for this expenditure of austerity; we are content with our own sacrifices, and we desire only what comes by righteous means.'

sanskrit: yajñān dīkṣās tathā homān yac cānyan mṛgayāmahe tan no 'stu svakṛtair yajñair nānyato mṛgayāmahe
english: 'Sacrifices, consecrations, oblations, and whatever else we seek—let that be ours through sacrifices of our own making; we do not seek it from elsewhere.'
